newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast spot power slips amid mild weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast spot power slips amid mild weather.

text.p: U.S. Southeast spot electricity prices ended Thursday mixed against Wednesday's level amid mild weather and flat power demand in the region, market sources said.
"Weather's cool...We have plenty of power," said one regional utility trader.

In the Southeastern Reliability Council (SERC), non-firm power for heavy demand hours on Friday into the northern portion of Tennessee Valley Authority's (TVA) system was offered in the $16.50 per megawatt hour area, compared with Wednesday's range of $14.75-$15.00.
But some SERC participants said pre-scheduled peak bulk power for Friday in northern TVA could be acquired in the $13.00-$13.50 area.
Weekend power prices at northern TVA were quoted at $15.00-$16.00.
Non-firm, peak electricity for delivery Friday in the southern part of TVA was valued at $16.00-$17.00, down from Wednesday's $17.00-$17.50.
Power prices for non-firm, peak delivery on Friday at the Florida/Georgia interface were assessed at $19.50-$20.50, down from $20.50-$21.00, and non-firm, off-peak delivery $14.00-$14.50.
Florida Power Corp's 825 MW Crystal River 3 nuclear unit in Red Level. Fla., remained shut following repairs to a leaky section of line that feeds lubrication oil to the unit's turbine shaft.
